newsitem.title: USA: Astra Merck ulcer bacteria test can claim more.
newsitem.headline: Astra Merck ulcer bacteria test can claim more.

text.p: Astra Merck Inc said Monday HpChek, a test to confirm the presence of H. pylori bacteria in patients with duodenal ulcer, received U.S. Food and Drug Administration 510K clearance for improved performance claims.
Astra Merck is a joint venture between Sweden's Astra Ab and U.S. pharmaceutical company Merck and Co.
HpChek is a one-step test conducted in a physician's office which confirms the presence of H. pylori, the bacterium believed to cause about 90 percent of duodenal ulcers.
The test was developed by ChemTrak Inc and would be marketed by Astra Merck starting in April as a companion product for Prilosec, its drug to treat acid-related disorders, the company said.
Before, H. pylori detection often required invasive clinical laboratory methods, the company said.

In an independent study HpChek demonstrated a relative sensitivity of 91 percent in biopsy positive specimens, a relative specificity of 98 percent in biopsy negative specimens and a relative agreement of 95 percent using fingerstick specimens compared to an enzyme-linked immunosorbant assay.
